mp_active_foci

Source: R/mp_active_foci.R
mp_active_foci.Rd

Identifies the active dengue transmission foci of a locality and the blocks (manzanas) to control, using a space-time window: cases within the flight range of *Aedes aegypti* (`spatial_scale`) and within the intrinsic + extrinsic incubation periods (`temporal_scale`).

mp_active_foci(
  geocoded_dataset,
  cve_edo,
  locality,
  status_caso = c(1, 2),
  spatial_scale = 400,
  temporal_scale = 21,
  min_cases = 3,
  buffer_m = 200,
  ref_date = NULL,
  method = c("window", "st-dbscan"),
  n_sim = 999,
  perm_days = 365,
  alpha = 0.05,
  seed = NULL,
  place = c("REP", "RES"),
  mean_si = 21,
  std_si = 6.1,
  capacity_cases = NULL,
  coverage_min = NULL,
  foci_min = 0.9,
  print_map = TRUE,
  save = FALSE,
  dir = "./"
)

Arguments

geocoded_dataset

data.table or data.frame with the geocoded cases. It must have the columns `long`, `lat` (EPSG:4326), `ESTATUS_CASO` and `FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT` (date of onset of symptoms).

cve_edo

INEGI state code of the locality (e.g. `"31"`).

locality

name of the locality, as used by [rgeomex::extract_locality()] (e.g. `"Merida"`).

status_caso

case status to use: 1 probable, 2 confirmed (default `c(1, 2)`).

spatial_scale

spatial window in metres: flight range of *Aedes aegypti* (default 400).

temporal_scale

temporal window in days: intrinsic + extrinsic incubation periods (default 21).

min_cases

minimum number of cases within the space-time window to define a focus (default 3).

buffer_m

buffer for control around the transmission zone, in metres (default 200; about 100 m is one block).

ref_date

reference date (`Date` or `"YYYY-MM-DD"`). The cases with onset in the `temporal_scale` days up to this date are used. If NULL (default), the latest date of onset in the locality is used.

method

how the foci are identified:

`"window"`

(default) fixed window: only the cases of the last `temporal_scale` days are used, and DBSCAN is applied with neighbours within `spatial_scale` metres. Answers "where are the foci today?".

`"st-dbscan"`

space-time DBSCAN: all the cases up to `ref_date` are used, and two cases are neighbours if they are within `spatial_scale` metres AND within `temporal_scale` days. It rebuilds the transmission chains, so a focus can last several weeks. Active foci are those with at least one case in the last `temporal_scale` days; they are classified as new (started in the window) or persistent (started before).

n_sim

number of permutations of the Knox test (default 999; 0 skips the test).

perm_days

period, in days up to `ref_date`, of the cases used by the Knox test (their dates are permuted; default 365). It is also the period used by `method = "st-dbscan"`. Must be >= `temporal_scale`.

alpha

significance level of the Knox test by focus, compared with the Holm-adjusted p-value (default 0.05).

seed

seed of the permutations, to reproduce the p-values (default NULL).

place

place used to select the cases of the locality for Rt with [rt_dengue()]: `"REP"` place of report (default; the cases are geocoded with it) or `"RES"` place of residence.

mean_si, std_si

mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval of dengue, gamma distribution, used to estimate Rt with [rt_dengue()] (default 21 and 6.1).

capacity_cases

operational capacity: number of cases per week that the brigades can work (the house of the case and the houses around it). It is local information given by the expert (default NULL, not evaluated). Used in the diagnosis to tell whether the outbreak exceeds the operational capacity (barrido vs operativo integral).

coverage_min

minimum proportion (0-1) of the locality covered by the recent cases (circles of `spatial_scale` metres) to consider the cases dispersed over the locality. NULL (default) depends on `temporal_scale`: 0.40 with 21 days or less, 0.50 with 28 days or more, and linear in between (calibrated with 71 localities, 2026; the coverage grows with the window).

foci_min

proportion (0-1) of the recent cases in foci from which the cases are also considered dispersed over the locality, whatever the coverage (default 0.9; safeguard for large cities, where the coverage is low even when the transmission covers the whole urban area).

print_map

logical. If TRUE (default) the map is printed; FALSE is useful in loops over several localities or dates (the map is still returned in `map`).

save

logical. If TRUE the selected blocks are saved as a GeoPackage in `dir` (default FALSE).

dir

directory where the blocks are saved (with "/" at the end).

Value

a list (invisibly) with:

map

interactive map (mapgl), also printed.

foci

sf with one row per active focus: type (new/persistent), cases, recent cases (in the window), confirmed cases, Knox pairs, expected pairs and RR, p-value, Holm p-value and significance, first and last onset, duration (days), transmission and control areas (km2) and number of blocks; geometry = control zone.

transmission

sf with the transmission zone of each focus.

blocks

sf with the blocks to control and their focus.

cases

sf with the cases of the window (and, with ST-DBSCAN, the previous cases of the active foci), their focus (NA if isolated) and group.

knox

global Knox test: list with the number of permutations (`n_sim`), the period (`periodo`), the number of cases (`n_casos`), the pairs within `spatial_scale` (`pares_espacio`), the Knox statistic (`knox`), the expected pairs (`esperados`), `rr`, `p_value` and the Knox statistic of each permutation (`sim`); NULL if `n_sim = 0`.

diagnostico

diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario: one-row summary (`tabla`, to bind several localities), scenario (`escenario`), operational strategy (`accion`), detail of the criteria (`detalle`, also printed), Rt by weekly sliding windows (`rt`, object of [EpiEstim::estimate_R()]) and its plot (`rt_plot`), cases by window of `temporal_scale` days (`casos_ventana`, the first is the current window), cases by month (`casos_mes`), proportion of the pairs of cases within `temporal_scale` days (`pct_pares_tiempo`), coverage of the locality by the recent cases (`cobertura_casos`), recent cases in foci (`pct_casos_en_focos`) and area of the transmission zones (`pct_area_transmision`).

Details

The foci are identified with the DBSCAN criterion:

  1. Temporal window: the window is the `temporal_scale` days up to `ref_date` (both included). With `method = "window"` only these cases are used; with `method = "st-dbscan"` all the cases up to `ref_date` are used and the time difference is part of the neighbourhood.

  2. Spatial window: a case is a *core* case if there are at least `min_cases` neighbours (itself included) within `spatial_scale` metres (and within `temporal_scale` days with ST-DBSCAN). Neighbouring core cases belong to the same focus, and non-core neighbours of a core case join that focus.

  3. Transmission zone: union of circles of `spatial_scale` metres around the cases of each focus in the window.

  4. Control zone: transmission zone plus `buffer_m` metres. The blocks that intersect the control zone are selected.

Knox test (space-time interaction; Knox 1964): the Knox statistic is the number of pairs of cases of the last `perm_days` days that are within `spatial_scale` metres and within `temporal_scale` days of each other, the same space-time window that defines the foci (and the same statistic as `denhotspots::knox_test()`). Its null distribution is obtained by permutation: the locations stay fixed (so the spatial distribution of the population is respected) and the dates of onset are permuted at random (so the epidemic curve is respected). p-value = (1 + permutations with as many pairs or more) / (`n_sim` + 1); RR = observed pairs / mean of the permuted pairs.

  1. Global test: all the pairs of the period. It answers whether the cases of the locality are closer in space and time than expected by chance. It is a formal test.

  2. Test by focus: only the pairs with both cases inside the transmission zone of the focus, with the dates permuted among all the cases of the period; p-values adjusted with Holm (`p_holm`). The foci were selected because their cases are close in space and time, so these p-values are optimistic: use them to rank and prioritise the foci, not as a formal test.

Unlike the size of the largest focus, the number of pairs does not percolate: in a dense city the permuted dates do not join more cases into the same pairs.

Diagnosis of the epidemiological scenario (`diagnostico`). Following dengue outbreak experts, transmission becomes generalised with:

  1. A sustained and significant increase of the outbreak: the cases of the current window are significantly above the mean per window of `temporal_scale` days of the period (Poisson test, p < `alpha`), the previous window is also above that mean and the effective reproductive number of the current window is above 1 (Rt with [rt_dengue()]: all the cases reported in the locality, `place`, geocoded or not; parametric serial interval with `mean_si` and `std_si`; Cori et al. 2013). Rt is ignored if it cannot be estimated.

  2. Cases that exceed the operational capacity: the cases per week of the current window (all the cases, probable and confirmed) are more than `capacity_cases`.

  3. Cases dispersed over the locality: the area within `spatial_scale` metres of the recent cases covers `coverage_min` or more of the locality, or `foci_min` or more of the recent cases are in foci.

The phase of the outbreak is given by the 95% credible interval of Rt: "En ascenso" (lower limit > 1), "En descenso" (upper limit < 1) or "Estable".

Scenarios (rules of thumb calibrated with 71 localities, 2026):

  1. Insufficient cases: fewer than 50 cases in the period.

  2. Generalised transmission: criterion 1 and (2 or 3). Strategy: barrido; operativo integral (megaoperativo) if the blocks exceed the operational capacity.

  3. No active foci. Strategy: entomological surveillance and control around the cases.

  4. Focalised transmission: 50% or more of the recent cases in foci. Strategy: focalised control, prioritising the significant foci.

  5. Focalised transmission with dispersed cases: fewer than 50% of the recent cases in foci. Strategy: focalised control and control around the isolated cases.

With criterion 1 and Rt in ascent ("En ascenso") but without generalised transmission, the action starts with an early warning (alerta temprana). The space-time interaction (Knox) is reported as "Sí" (p < `alpha`), "No concluyente" (RR > 1.05) or "No". The strategies summarise the "Resumen de Estrategias Operativas" (focalizado, barrido, operativo integral). Areas are clipped to the locality.

DBSCAN is run with the dbscan package (Hahsler, Piekenbrock and Doran 2019): [dbscan::frNN()] finds the neighbours within `spatial_scale` metres and, with ST-DBSCAN, the neighbours further than `temporal_scale` days are removed before [dbscan::dbscan()] is applied with `minPts = min_cases`. Distances are computed in metres (EPSG:6372, Mexico ITRF2008 / LCC). Blocks come from `rgeomex::blocks_ine20_mx_*` (INE 2020). The map opens with the Positron style (OpenFreeMap); a collapsible layers control turns on and off the basemaps (Esri Dark Gray, Esri Light Gray, OpenStreetMap, World Imagery, OpenTopoMap) and the zones, blocks and cases. The transmission zone of each focus is coloured by its Knox test: red, significant (Holm p-value < `alpha`); yellow, excess of pairs not significant (RR > 1); grey, no excess (RR <= 1). With `n_sim = 0` all the zones are red.

References

Cori A, Ferguson NM, Fraser C, Cauchemez S (2013). A new framework and software to estimate time-varying reproduction numbers during epidemics. *American Journal of Epidemiology*, 178(9), 1505-1512.

Knox EG (1964). The detection of space-time interactions. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C*, 13(1), 25-30.

Kulldorff M, Hjalmars U (1999). The Knox method and other tests for space-time interaction. *Biometrics*, 55(2), 544-552.

Hahsler M, Piekenbrock M, Doran D (2019). dbscan: Fast Density-Based Clustering with R. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 91(1), 1-30. doi:10.18637/jss.v091.i01

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- mp_active_foci(geocoded_dataset = z,
                      cve_edo = "31",
                      locality = "Merida",
                      status_caso = c(1, 2),
                      spatial_scale = 400,
                      temporal_scale = 21,
                      min_cases = 3,
                      buffer_m = 200,
                      ref_date = NULL,
                      method = "window",
                      n_sim = 999,
                      perm_days = 365,
                      alpha = 0.05,
                      seed = 123,
                      place = "REP",
                      mean_si = 21,
                      std_si = 6.1,
                      capacity_cases = NULL,
                      coverage_min = NULL,
                      foci_min = 0.9,
                      print_map = TRUE,
                      save = FALSE,
                      dir = "./")
res$foci      # summary of the foci
res$blocks    # blocks to control
res$knox      # global Knox test
hist(res$knox$sim)                      # null distribution of the pairs
abline(v = res$knox$knox, col = "red")  # observed pairs
res$diagnostico$tabla       # scenario, criteria and action
res$diagnostico$casos_mes   # cases by month of the period

# space-time DBSCAN: transmission chains, new and persistent foci
res_st <- mp_active_foci(geocoded_dataset = z,
                         cve_edo = "31",
                         locality = "Merida",
                         status_caso = c(1, 2),
                         spatial_scale = 400,
                         temporal_scale = 21,
                         min_cases = 3,
                         buffer_m = 200,
                         ref_date = NULL,
                         method = "st-dbscan",
                         n_sim = 999,
                         perm_days = 365,
                         alpha = 0.05,
                         seed = 123,
                         place = "REP",
                         mean_si = 21,
                         std_si = 6.1,
                         capacity_cases = NULL,
                         coverage_min = NULL,
                         foci_min = 0.9,
                         print_map = TRUE,
                         save = FALSE,
                         dir = "./")
} # }
